  if json_member "$document" "$slot" expires_at && \
      [[ "$json_type" == number && "$json_value" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    expires="$json_value"
  fi
  printf '%s\x1f%s\n' "$access" "$expires"
}

grant_access_token() {
  local access
  access="$(json_fields "$1" access_token)" || return 1
  [[ -n "$access" ]] || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "$access"
}

ensure_access_token() {
  local fields access expires_at
  if [[ -n "$access_token" ]]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$access_token"
    return 0
  fi
  fields="$(read_credential)" || return 1
  IFS=$'\x1f' read -r access expires_at <<<"$fields"
  [[ -n "$access" ]] || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "$access"
}

download_auth_header() {
  local token
  [[ "$skip_download_auth" == 0 ]] || return 0
  case "$1" in
    "https://$download_host/"*) ;;
    *) return 0 ;;
  esac
  token=***

|| return 0
  [[ -n "$token" ]] || return 0
  printf 'Authorization: *** %s\n' "$token"
}

# Emits the granted access token on stdout; every human-facing line goes to
# stderr, so the caller can capture the token without swallowing the prompts.
device_login() (
  local auth_work="" response status fields
  local device_code user_code verification_uri verification_uri_complete
  local lifetime interval deadline error
  local minutes expiry bold="" normal=""

  trap '[[ -z "$auth_work" ]] || rm -rf "$auth_work"' EXIT
  auth_work="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/muse-login.XXXXXX")" || return 1
  response="$auth_work/device.json"

  status="$(auth_post "$authorization_endpoint" "$response" \
    "client_id=$client_id")" || return 1
  case "$status" in
    2??) ;;
    3??)
      printf 'muse: the sign-in service redirected the request; not following it\n' >&2
      return 1
      ;;
    404)
      printf 'muse: sign-in is not available yet\n' >&2
      return 1
      ;;
    *)
      printf 'muse: sign-in could not be started (HTTP %s)\n' "$status" >&2
      return 1
      ;;
  esac

  fields="$(json_fields "$response" \
    device_code \
    user_code \
    verification_uri \
    verification_uri_complete \
    expires_in \
    interval)" || return 1
  IFS=$'\x1f' read -r device_code user_code verification_uri \
    verification_uri_complete lifetime interval <<<"$fields"
  [[ -n "$device_code" && -n "$user_code" ]] || return 1
  verification_uri="$(normalize_https_url "$verification_uri")" || return 1
  if [[ -n "$verification_uri_complete" ]]; then
    verification_uri_complete="$(
      normalize_https_url "$verification_uri_complete"
    )" || verification_uri_complete=""
  fi
  [[ "$interval" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && ((interval > 0)) || interval=5
  [[ "$lifetime" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || lifetime=900
  ((lifetime >= 60)) || lifetime=60
  ((lifetime <= 1800)) || lifetime=1800
  deadline=$(($(date +%s) + lifetime))

  if [[ -t 2 && -z "${NO_COLOR:-}" ]]; then
    if ! { bold="$(tput bold 2>/dev/null)" && \
        normal="$(tput sgr0 2>/dev/null)"; }; then
      bold=""
      normal=""
    fi
  fi

  printf '\n' >&2
  printf 'Open this page to sign in:\n' >&2
  printf '  %s\n' "${verification_uri_complete:-$verification_uri}" >&2
  if [[ -n "$verification_uri_complete" ]]; then
    printf 'Confirm this code matches:\n' >&2
  else
    printf 'Enter this code:\n' >&2
  fi
  printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$bold" "$user_code" "$normal" >&2
  printf '\n' >&2
  confirm_open_verification_page \
    "${verification_uri_complete:-$verification_uri}"
  minutes=$(((lifetime + 59) / 60))
  expiry="$minutes minutes"
  ((minutes != 1)) || expiry='1 minute'
  printf 'Waiting for approval (link expires in %s)... ' "$expiry" >&2

  response="$auth_work/token.json"
  while :; do
    if (($(date +%s) >= deadline)); then
      printf '\nmuse: the sign-in request expired before it was approved\n' >&2
      return 1
    fi
    status="$(auth_post "$token_endpoint" "$response" \
      "grant_type=$device_code_grant" \
      "device_code=$device_code" \
      "client_id=$client_id")" || { printf '\n' >&2; return 1; }
    case "$status" in
      2??)
        grant_access_token "$response" || {
          printf '\nmuse: the sign-in response carried no usable token\n' >&2
          return 1
        }
        printf 'Signed in.\n' >&2
        return 0
        ;;
      3??)
        printf '\nmuse: the sign-in service redirected the request; not following it\n' >&2
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
    error="$(json_fields "$response" error 2>/dev/null || true)"
    case "$error" in
      authorization_pending) ;;
      slow_down) interval=$((interval + 5)) ;;
      access_denied)
        printf '\nmuse: the sign-in request was denied\n' >&2
        return 1
        ;;
      expired_token)
        printf '\nmuse: the sign-in request expired before it was approved\n' >&2
        return 1
        ;;
      *)
        printf '\nmuse: sign-in failed (HTTP %s)\n' "$status" >&2
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
    sleep "$interval"
  done
)

login_after_denial() {
  if [[ "${MUSE_LOGIN:-}" == 0 ]]; then
    return 1
  fi
  if [[ "${MUSE_LOGIN:-}" != 1 && ! -t 2 ]]; then
    return 1
  fi
  access_token=***

|| {
    access_token=***

return 1
  }
}

fetch_json() {
  local url="$1"
  local destination="$2"
  local header
  local extra=()
  header="$(download_auth_header "$url")"
  [[ -z "$header" ]] || extra=(--header "$header")
  curl \
    --silent \
    --show-error \
    --location \
    --max-redirs 3 \
    --proto '=https' \
    --proto-redir '=https' \
    --tlsv1.2 \
    --user-agent "$user_agent" \
    --header 'Accept: application/json' \
    "${extra[@]+"${extra[@]}"}" \
    --output "$destination" \
    --write-out '%{http_code}' \
    "$url"
}

fetch_launcher() {
  curl \
    --silent \
    --show-error \
    --location \
    --max-redirs 3 \
    --proto '=https' \
    --proto-redir '=https' \
    --tlsv1.2 \
    --connect-timeout 10 \
    --max-time 60 \
    --user-agent "$user_agent" \
    --dump-header "$3" \
    --output "$2" \
    --write-out '%{http_code}' \
    "$1"
}

fetch_artifact() {
  local url="$1"
  local destination="$2"
  local header
  local extra=()
  header="$(download_auth_header "$url")"
  [[ -z "$header" ]] || extra=(--header "$header")
  if [[ -t 2 ]]; then
    curl \
      --show-error \
      --location \
      --max-redirs 3 \
      --proto '=https' \
      --proto-redir '=https' \
      --tlsv1.2 \
      --user-agent "$user_agent" \
      --progress-bar \
      "${extra[@]+"${extra[@]}"}" \
      --output "$destination" \
      --write-out '%{http_code}' \
      "$url"
  else
    curl \
      --silent \
      --show-error \
      --location \
      --max-redirs 3 \
      --proto '=https' \
      --proto-redir '=https' \
      --tlsv1.2 \
      --user-agent "$user_agent" \
      "${extra[@]+"${extra[@]}"}" \
      --output "$destination" \
      --write-out '%{http_code}' \
      "$url"
  fi
}

is_auth_denial() {
  case "$1" in
    401|403|404) return 0 ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}

fetch_json_with_login() {
  local url="$1" destination="$2" had_auth=0
  [[ -z "$(download_auth_header "$url")" ]] || had_auth=1
  skip_download_auth=1
  request_status="$(fetch_json "$url" "$destination")" || {
    skip_download_auth=0
    return 1
  }
  skip_download_auth=0
  if is_auth_denial "$request_status" && ((had_auth != 0)); then
    request_status="$(fetch_json "$url" "$destination")" || {
      return 1
    }
  fi
  if is_auth_denial "$request_status" && login_after_denial; then
    request_status="$(fetch_json "$url" "$destination")" || return 1
  fi
}

fetch_artifact_with_login() {
  local url="$1" destination="$2" had_auth=0
  [[ -z "$(download_auth_header "$url")" ]] || had_auth=1
  skip_download_auth=1
  request_status="$(fetch_artifact "$url" "$destination")" || {
    skip_download_auth=0
    return 1

  skip_download_auth=0

      return 1
    }
  fi

die_http() {
  local status="$1"
  local url="$2"
  case "$status" in
    401)
      die "the download was rejected (HTTP 401); rerun the installer to sign in again"
      ;;
    403)
      die "the download was refused (HTTP 403); muse is available to Meta employees"
      ;;
    *) die "request failed (HTTP $status): $url" ;;
  esac

acquire_lock() {
  local dir="$1"
  local lock_pid
  lock_dir="$dir/.muse-update-lock"
  if [[ -d "$lock_dir" ]]; then
    lock_pid=""
    [[ ! -r "$lock_dir/pid" ]] || lock_pid="$(<"$lock_dir/pid")"
    if [[ ! "$lock_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || \
        ! kill -0 "$lock_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
      rm -rf -- "$lock_dir"
    fi
  fi
  mkdir -- "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "$$" >"$lock_dir/pid"
}

# Final response only: --location dumps one header block per response.
read_response_header() {
  local file="$1" wanted="$2" line name value=""
  [[ -r "$file" ]] || return 0
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    line="${line%$'\r'}"
    if [[ "$line" == HTTP/* ]]; then
      value=""
      continue
    fi
    [[ "$line" == *:* ]] || continue
    name="$(printf '%s' "${line%%:*}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
    [[ "$name" == "$wanted" ]] || continue
    value="${line#*:}"
  done <"$file"
  while [[ "$value" == [[:space:]]* ]]; do value="${value#?}"; done
  while [[ "$value" == *[[:space:]] ]]; do value="${value%?}"; done
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
}

# Replaces this script when a newer one is published. Rename, never write:
# bash reads a script as it runs, so overwriting a live launcher corrupts it.
# Best effort -- any failure leaves the current launcher in place.
_update_launcher() {
  local self="$1" dir published current advertised status
  dir="$(parent_directory "$self")"
  [[ -w "$self" && -w "$dir" ]] || return 1
  launcher_tmp="$(mktemp "$dir/.muse-launcher.XXXXXX")" || return 1
  launcher_headers="$launcher_tmp.headers"
  status="$(fetch_launcher "$launcher_url" "$launcher_tmp" \
    "$launcher_headers")" || return 1
  [[ "$status" == 2?? ]] || return 1

  # A body that cannot parse must never reach the launcher; there is no recovery.
  bash -n "$launcher_tmp" 2>/dev/null || return 1

  published="$(sha256_file "$launcher_tmp")" || return 1
  published="$(printf '%s' "$published" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"

  # Verified when advertised; older serving code sends none.
  advertised="$(read_response_header "$launcher_headers" x-content-sha256)"
  advertised="$(printf '%s' "$advertised" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
  if [[ "$advertised" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]]; then
    [[ "$published" == "$advertised" ]] || return 1
  fi

  current="$(sha256_file "$self")" || return 1
  current="$(printf '%s' "$current" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
  [[ "$published" != "$current" ]] || return 1

  cp -f -- "$self" "$dir/.muse-launcher.previous" 2>/dev/null || true
  # Checked explicitly: set -e is off here, this runs as the left side of `||`.
  chmod -- 0755 "$launcher_tmp" || return 1
  mv -f -- "$launcher_tmp" "$self" || return 1
  launcher_tmp=""
  return 0
}

# Subshell with traps, like update_binary: an interrupted download must not
# strand temp files in the install dir, and nothing in here may stop the run --
# `|| true` alone does not contain a set -u abort.
discard_launcher_download() {
  [[ -z "$launcher_tmp" ]] || rm -f -- "$launcher_tmp"
  launcher_tmp=""
  [[ -z "$launcher_headers" ]] || rm -f -- "$launcher_headers"
  launcher_headers=""
}

update_launcher() (
  trap discard_launcher_download EXIT
  trap 'exit 129' HUP
  trap 'exit 130' INT
  trap 'exit 143' TERM
  _update_launcher "$1" || true
)

# Background updates finish after the handoff, so leave a note for the next run.
# An undelivered note keeps its original starting version.
record_update_notice() {
  local dir="$1" from="$2" to="$3"
  local notice pending
  [[ -n "$from" && "$from" != "$to" ]] || return 0
  notice="$dir/.muse-update-notice"
  pending=""
  [[ ! -r "$notice" ]] || pending="$(<"$notice")"
  [[ "$pending" != *$'\t'* ]] || from="${pending%%$'\t'*}"
  if [[ "$from" == "$to" ]]; then
    rm -f -- "$notice"
    return
  fi
  notice_tmp="$notice.tmp.$$"
  if ! printf '%s\t%s\n' "$from" "$to" >"$notice_tmp"; then
    rm -f -- "$notice_tmp"
    notice_tmp=""
    return 1
  fi
  if ! mv -f -- "$notice_tmp" "$notice"; then
    rm -f -- "$notice_tmp"
    notice_tmp=""
    return 1
  fi
  notice_tmp=""
}

publish_release_info() {
  local dir="$1" source="$2" release_info
  release_info="$dir/.muse-release-info.json"
  release_info_tmp="$release_info.tmp.$$"
  mv -f -- "$source" "$release_info_tmp"
  mv -f -- "$release_info_tmp" "$release_info"
  release_info_tmp=""
}

)

update_binary() (

    return 0

    die "could not reach $manifest_url"
  status="$request_status"
  [[ "$status" == 2?? ]] || die_http "$status" "$manifest_url"
  platform="$(detect_platform)"

    "$release_manifest" "$version" "$platform")" || \

    die "could not reach $artifact_url"

    die "artifact size mismatch: expected $expected_size, got $actual_size"

  mv -f -- "$candidate" "$target"
  publish_release_info "$dir" "$channel_manifest"
  state_tmp="$state.tmp.$$"
  printf '%s\n' "$version" >"$state_tmp"
  mv -f -- "$state_tmp" "$state"
  state_tmp=""
  record_update_notice "$dir" "$installed_version" "$version"

  shopt -s nullglob
  for old_binary in "$dir"/muse-bin-*; do
    [[ "$old_binary" == "$target" ]] || rm -f "$old_binary"
  done
  rm -f -- "$dir/muse-bin"
)

active_binary() {
  local dir="$1"
  local version

  [[ ! -r "$dir/.muse-version" ]] || version="$(<"$dir/.muse-version")"
  [[ "$version" =~ $version_pattern ]] || return 1
  printf '%s/muse-bin-%s\n' "$dir" "$version"
}

release_info_for_active_binary() {
  local dir="$1" state release_info installed_version
  local manifest_values version manifest_url
  state="$dir/.muse-version"
  release_info="$dir/.muse-release-info.json"
  [[ -r "$state" && -r "$release_info" ]] || return 1
  installed_version="$(<"$state")"
  manifest_values="$(parse_channel_manifest "$release_info")" || return 1
  IFS=$'\t' read -r version manifest_url <<<"$manifest_values"
  [[ "$version" == "$installed_version" ]] || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "$(<"$release_info")"
}

# Claims a note atomically. Malformed notes are consumed so they cannot wedge.
main() {
  local dir binary checked_at checked_tmp now release_info
  case "$channel" in
    muse-stable|muse-canary) ;;
    *) die "unsupported channel: $channel" ;;
  esac
  dir="$(resolve_install_dir)"
  checked_at="$dir/.muse-update-checked-at"

  if [[ "${MUSE_LAUNCHER_INSTALL:-0}" == 1 ]]; then
    update_binary "$dir"
    binary="$(active_binary "$dir")" || \
      die "installation did not produce an active binary"
    [[ -x "$binary" ]] || die "installed binary is missing: $binary"
    report_update_notice "$dir"
    exit 0
  fi

  binary="$(active_binary "$dir" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [[ ! -x "$binary" ]]; then
    if [[ "${MUSE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE:-0}" == 1 ]]; then
      die "installed binary is missing; rerun the installer"
    fi
    update_launcher "$(resolve_self)" || true
    update_binary "$dir"
    binary="$(active_binary "$dir")" || \
      die "installed binary is missing; rerun the installer"
  elif [[ "${MUSE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE:-0}" != 1 ]] && \
      should_check_for_update "$checked_at"; then
    now="$(date +%s)"
    checked_tmp="$checked_at.tmp.$$"
    if printf '%s\n' "$now" >"$checked_tmp" && \
        mv -f -- "$checked_tmp" "$checked_at"; then
      if [[ "${MUSE_SYNC_UPDATE:-0}" == 1 ]]; then
        update_launcher "$(resolve_self)" || true
        update_binary "$dir"
        binary="$(active_binary "$dir")" || \
          die "installed binary is missing; rerun the installer"
      else
        ({ update_launcher "$(resolve_self)" || true; update_binary "$dir"; } \
          </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &)
      fi
    fi
  fi

  report_update_notice "$dir"
  release_info="$(release_info_for_active_binary "$dir" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [[ -n "$release_info" ]]; then
    export MUSE_RELEASE_INFO="$release_info"
  else
    unset MUSE_RELEASE_INFO
  fi
  exec "$binary" "$@"
}

main "$@"

active_binary() {
  local dir="$1"
  local version

  [[ "$version" =~ $version_pattern ]] || return 1

}

release_info_for_active_binary() {
  local dir="$1" state release_info installed_version
  local manifest_values version manifest_url
  state="$dir/.muse-version"
  release_info="$dir/.muse-release-info.json"
  [[ -r "$state" && -r "$release_info" ]] || return 1
  installed_version="$(<"$state")"
  manifest_values="$(parse_channel_manifest "$release_info")" || return 1
  IFS=$'\t' read -r version manifest_url <<<"$manifest_values"

}

main() {
  local dir binary checked_at checked_tmp now release_info

    muse-stable|muse-canary) ;;

  dir="$(resolve_install_dir)"
  checked_at="$dir/.muse-update-checked-at"

  if [[ "${MUSE_LAUNCHER_INSTALL:-0}" == 1 ]]; then
    update_binary "$dir"
    binary="$(active_binary "$dir")" || \
      die "installation did not produce an active binary"

    report_update_notice "$dir"
    exit 0
  fi

  binary="$(active_binary "$dir" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [[ ! -x "$binary" ]]; then
    if [[ "${MUSE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE:-0}" == 1 ]]; then
      die "installed binary is missing; rerun the installer"
    fi
    update_launcher "$(resolve_self)" || true
    update_binary "$dir"
    binary="$(active_binary "$dir")" || \
      die "installed binary is missing; rerun the installer"
  elif [[ "${MUSE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE:-0}" != 1 ]] && \
      should_check_for_update "$checked_at"; then
    now="$(date +%s)"
    checked_tmp="$checked_at.tmp.$$"
    if printf '%s\n' "$now" >"$checked_tmp" && \
        mv -f -- "$checked_tmp" "$checked_at"; then
      if [[ "${MUSE_SYNC_UPDATE:-0}" == 1 ]]; then
        update_launcher "$(resolve_self)" || true
        update_binary "$dir"
        binary="$(active_binary "$dir")" || \
          die "installed binary is missing; rerun the installer"
      else
        ({ update_launcher "$(resolve_self)" || true; update_binary "$dir"; } \
          </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &)
      fi
    fi
  fi

  report_update_notice "$dir"
  release_info="$(release_info_for_active_binary "$dir" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [[ -n "$release_info" ]]; then
    export MUSE_RELEASE_INFO="$release_info"
  else
    unset MUSE_RELEASE_INFO
  fi
  exec "$binary" "$@"
}

device_login() (
  local auth_work="" response status fields
  local device_code user_code verification_uri verification_uri_complete
  local lifetime interval deadline error
  local minutes expiry bold="" normal=""

  trap '[[ -z "$auth_work" ]] || rm -rf "$auth_work"' EXIT
  auth_work="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/muse-login.XXXXXX")" || return 1
  response="$auth_work/device.json"

  status="$(auth_post "$authorization_endpoint" "$response" \
    "client_id=$client_id")" || return 1
  case "$status" in
    2??) ;;
    3??)
      printf 'muse: the sign-in service redirected the request; not following it\n' >&2
      return 1
      ;;
    404)
      printf 'muse: sign-in is not available yet\n' >&2
      return 1
      ;;
    *)
      printf 'muse: sign-in could not be started (HTTP %s)\n' "$status" >&2
      return 1
      ;;
  esac

  fields="$(json_fields "$response" \
    device_code \
    user_code \
    verification_uri \
  expiry="$minutes minutes"
  ((minutes != 1)) || expiry='1 minute'
  printf 'Waiting for approval (link expires in %s)... ' "$expiry" >&2

  response="$auth_work/token.json"
  while :; do
    if (($(date +%s) >= deadline)); then
      printf '\nmuse: the sign-in request expired before it was approved\n' >&2
      return 1
    fi
    status="$(auth_post "$token_endpoint" "$response" \
      "grant_type=$device_code_grant" \
      "device_code=$device_code" \
      "client_id=$client_id")" || { printf '\n' >&2; return 1; }
    case "$status" in
      2??)
        grant_access_token "$response" || {
          printf '\nmuse: the sign-in response carried no usable token\n' >&2
          return 1
        }
        printf 'Signed in.\n' >&2
        return 0
        ;;
      3??)
        printf '\nmuse: the sign-in service redirected the request; not following it\n' >&2
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
    error="$(json_fields "$response" error 2>/dev/null || true)"
    case "$error" in
      authorization_pending) ;;
      slow_down) interval=$((interval + 5)) ;;
      access_denied)
        printf '\nmuse: the sign-in request was denied\n' >&2
        return 1
        ;;
      expired_token)
        printf '\nmuse: the sign-in request expired before it was approved\n' >&2
        return 1
        ;;
      *)
        printf '\nmuse: sign-in failed (HTTP %s)\n' "$status" >&2
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
    sleep "$interval"
  done
)

login_after_denial() {
  if [[ "${MUSE_LOGIN:-}" == 0 ]]; then
    return 1
  fi
  if [[ "${MUSE_LOGIN:-}" != 1 && ! -t 2 ]]; then
    return 1
  fi
  access_token=***

|| {
    access_token=***

I read the second-stage launcher (`muse-launcher.sh`, 1,126 lines) without running anything. Its sha256 matches the hash Meta's server advertises (`c6db2947…a4bc`). Nothing is installed: there are no files in `~/.local/bin` and no shell config changes.

**What the launcher does:**
- **Installs one binary.** It reads the channel file at `api.meta.ai/muse-code/channels/muse-stable` (currently `1.4.14-R7309.1`), then a release manifest on `lookaside.facebook.com`. It downloads the `x86_linux` binary to `~/.local/bin/muse-bin-<version>` and checks its size and sha256 against that manifest. It doesn't use `sudo`, add system services or cron jobs, or write outside `~/.local/bin` and `~/.config/muse/`.
- **Signs in to Meta.** If the download is refused, it starts a device-code sign-in at `auth.meta.com` and saves the token to `~/.config/muse/auth.json`. It only sends that token to `lookaside.facebook.com`.
- **Updates itself automatically.** By default, every time you run `muse` it checks for updates (at most once an hour), in the background. It replaces both the launcher and the binary, deletes older binary versions, and then runs the new binary. `MUSE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` turns this off.
- **Trust:** the binary's checksum is verified, but it comes from a manifest on the same Meta server, and there's no signature. So you're trusting Meta's servers and HTTPS, not an independent check. The file is HTTPS-only and won't fall back to plain HTTP.

**What I couldn't check:** the `muse` binary itself, which is what actually runs. The scripts are a careful, standard installer. The binary is a closed Meta program, and I haven't seen what it reads, sends out or changes. That's the part your restoration rule is really about.

**Recommendation:** don't install it on this host while the restoration is in progress. If you want it, install it on the laptop, or here only after the restoration. If you install it here anyway, I'd use `MUSE_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1 MUSE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` so it can't edit your shell files or update itself.

Both scripts are in `/tmp/claude-1000/-srv-git-odbus-verified/2595e343-c893-419f-b503-2e33af046481/scratchpad/metaai-install/`.

--max-cost=<value>                Stop sending model requests once the session's spend reaches this many USD; requests already in flight can finish past it (print mode exits 3)
  # Use different model (fuzzy matching)
    omp --model opus "Help me refactor this code"
  # Limit model cycling to specific models
    omp --models claude-sonnet,claude-haiku,gpt-4o
COMMANDS
  auth           Export or import stored provider credentials (API keys and OAuth logins) as JSON
  auth-broker    Manage the omp auth-broker (credential vault)
  auth-gateway   Run an auth-gateway: an HTTP forward proxy backed by the configured broker, or JSON lines on stdio with your own credentials
  bench          Benchmark models: TTFT/prefill vs decode throughput with p50/p95, across chat, prefill, generation, and prompt-cache workloads, or single-user vs parallel load (--detailed)
  dry-balance    Dry-run OAuth account balancing across random session ids
  login          Log in to a model provider (terminal counterpart of /login)
  models         List, search, and refresh available models
  search         Test web search providers
  tiny-models    Download tiny local models (session titles, memory, word completion)
  token          Get the API key or OAuth token for a provider
  usage          Show provider usage limits for every authenticated account
  # Core Providers
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY          - Anthropic Claude models
  ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN      - Anthropic OAuth (takes precedence over API key)
  ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY  - Anthropic token used as Authorization: *** <token> in Foundry mode
  OPENAI_API_KEY             - OpenAI GPT models
  GEMINI_API_KEY             - Google Gemini models

  GROQ_API_KEY               - Groq models
  CEREBRAS_API_KEY           - Cerebras models
  XAI_API_KEY                - xAI Grok models
  OPENROUTER_API_KEY         - OpenRouter aggregated models
  KILO_API_KEY               - Kilo Gateway models
  MISTRAL_API_KEY            - Mistral models
  ZAI_API_KEY                - z.ai models (ZhipuAI/GLM)

  CHARM_HYPER_API_KEY        - Charm Hyper inference gateway models

  YOLO_AUTO_API_KEY          - Yolo-Auto flat-rate Qwen models

List, search, and refresh available models

USAGE
  $ omp models [ACTION] [PATTERN] [FLAGS]

ARGUMENTS
  ACTION    ls (default) | find | refresh | <provider>
  PATTERN   Filter/search substring, or provider name (required for find)

FLAGS
      --json               Output JSON
      --kind=<value>       Catalog kind to list
  -e, --extension=<value>  Load an extension file before listing (repeatable)
      --no-extensions      Disable extension discovery (explicit -e paths still work)
      --config=<value>     Load an extra config.yml-style overlay for this run (repeatable)

EXAMPLES
  # List available chat models, grouped by provider
    omp models
  # List models of every catalog kind
    omp models --kind all
  # List one provider's models (any provider name works)
    omp models openai-codex
  # Find models by substring
    omp models find minimax
  # Force a fresh catalog fetch (replaces rm -rf ~/.omp/models.db)
    omp models refresh
  # Machine-readable output
    omp models --json

content.text:
Yes, you're right. The earlier sessions show direct calls to `api.meta.ai/v1` with the `META_API_KEY` from `~/.bash_secrets`:
- `GET /v1/models` returned HTTP 200 with an empty list (`"data": []`).
- `chat/completions` and `responses` returned `404 model_not_found` for `muse-spark-1.1`, `1.3` and `1.3-contributor`.
- omp's cache showed Meta had listed those models on 10-28 at 15:49 UTC. By 10-29 the list was empty.

The test I just ran with omp's default model failed the same way.

**Why muse might help:** muse doesn't use your API key. It signs in with your Meta account at `auth.meta.com`, and its binary refers to `api.meta.ai/muse-code/key` and `api.meta.ai/v1`. That suggests it gets its own key or token after you sign in, possibly tied to a Muse Code plan. If that one has models enabled, omp can use it. The binary also has `accountscenter.meta.com/muse_code/?ep=no_payg` links. My guess is that your old key lost access because model access now needs a plan or pay-as-you-go billing on the account. That would explain a list that empties out while the key itself is still accepted.

**The next step is yours:** I can't do the sign-in, because it needs a browser approval. In your own terminal, run:
```
muse
```
Approve the Meta link it shows, then tell me when you're signed in. I'll then:
1. Check what got saved in `~/.config/muse/` (without printing it), and ask Meta's `/v1/models` whether that credential lists any models.
2. If it does, point omp's `meta` provider at that credential and rerun the one-word test on `meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor`.

If `muse` itself shows an error or a billing page, paste it here, because that will be the real cause.

|---|---|
| through **23:53:10** | Meta calls succeed (`muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, `muse-spark-1.1`) |

- `~/.bash_secrets` was last edited at 17:38, and the same key worked for six hours after that.
- omp's `config.yml` was last changed at 01:37 on 10-29, after the failures started. `models.yml` hasn't changed since 10-24.

On Meta's side, the same key is still accepted (HTTP 200, not 401), but its model list is now empty. So the key wasn't deleted; its access to the models was removed on Meta's servers. That fits the `no_payg` billing link inside the muse binary. Your logs can't tell which one it was.

2. Or check the Meta developer console for this key's project: usage limits, billing and model access. Once this prints more than 0, omp will work again with no changes:

content.text:
Your original `AGENTS.md` is safe. `AGENTS.md.bk` (created at 02:15:20) is identical to the committed version, and the stub from `muse init` was written 8 seconds later. If you made that backup on purpose so muse could create its own file, nothing's wrong. If not, `mv AGENTS.md.bk AGENTS.md` puts it back. I haven't touched either file. Until it's back, Claude, Codex and the other agents only see the stub.

**Business account sign-in:** muse's login is a device-code flow at `auth.meta.com`. It always uses whichever Meta account is signed in in that browser and never shows an account picker, so there's no business option on the muse side. Ways to get to the business account:

1. **Sign in as the business account in the browser first.** In a fresh private window, go to `auth.meta.com` or `accountscenter.meta.com`, sign in with the business login (or switch to it in Accounts Center), then open the link muse prints. The approval will be for that account.
2. **Use a key from the business org.** On `dev.meta.ai`, open the business org/project and create an API key there. Then check it before switching anything:
   ```
   ! curl -s -H "Authorization: *** NEWKEY" https://api.meta.ai/v1/models | grep -c muse
   ```
   If that prints more than 0, put it on the `META_API_KEY` line in `~/.bash_secrets` and uncomment the three lines. omp and muse will both work with no other changes.
3. **If the business account isn't linked to the login you're using,** link it in Accounts Center first. Otherwise the device flow can't reach it.

Option 2 is the most direct way to get omp working again, because omp only uses an API key, not muse's sign-in.

content.text:
Third-party cookie blocking could well be the cause. Meta's sign-in moves between several Meta domains, like `auth.meta.com`, `accountscenter.meta.com` and `facebook.com`/`business.facebook.com`. Switching to a business or work account depends on those sites reading each other's cookies. When third-party cookies are blocked, the usual result is what you're seeing: the personal login works, but the business option never appears.

To test it, allow cookies for these sites only, rather than turning blocking off everywhere:
- `[*.]meta.com`
- `[*.]facebook.com`
- `[*.]meta.ai`

In Chrome or Brave that's Settings → Privacy → Third-party cookies → "Allowed to use third-party cookies". In Brave, also turn Shields off for those sites. In Firefox, add them as exceptions under Enhanced Tracking Protection.

Then reload the muse sign-in link. If the business option still doesn't appear, try a different browser with default settings. If it's missing there too, cookies aren't the cause, and the business account probably isn't linked to that login in Accounts Center.

content.text:
Here are steps to reproduce for the ticket:

---

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Sign in to dev.meta.ai as the business account (Team ID `4168260789970698`, Project ID `2206994009851358`).
2. Go to **API keys** and create a new key, then export it:
   ```
   export MODEL_API_KEY=*** key>
   ```
3. List the available models:
   ```
   curl -s https://api.meta.ai/v1/models -H "Authorization: *** $MODEL_API_KEY"
   ```
   **Expected:** a list including `muse-spark-1.3`, `muse-wonder-1.0`, etc.
   **Actual:** `{"object":"list","data":[]}` (HTTP 200)
4. Send a request using the dashboard's own sample code, through the Responses API:
   ```
   curl -s https://api.meta.ai/v1/responses \
     -H "Authorization: *** $MODEL_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"model":"muse-spark-1.3","input":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"Reply with exactly: ok"}]}],"stream":false}'
   ```
   **Expected:** a model response.
   **Actual:** HTTP 404
   `{"error":{"code":"model_not_found","message":"The requested model was not found.","param":null,"type":"invalid_request_error"}}`
5. Repeat step 4 with `muse-spark-1.1`, `muse-spark-1.2`, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` and `muse-wonder-1.0`. **Actual:** the same 404 for each, and the same on `/v1/chat/completions`.
6. Open the **Chat** page in the dev.meta.ai dashboard and send a message. **Actual:** it works normally.
7. Optionally, install the Muse Code CLI (1.4.14-R7309.1) and run `muse`. **Actual:** `failed to fetch model catalog: model catalog has no visible models`.

**Started:** 2026-10-28. API calls succeeded until 23:53:10 UTC and failed from 23:56:31 UTC on. Nothing changed on our side in between.

**Reproducible:** every time, with both the original key and a newly created one.

---

Step 4 says "using the dashboard's own sample code" because your pasted script came from there. I didn't run step 4 with your new key myself; my tests used the old key. Before sending, run step 3 or 4 with the new key in your terminal and make sure the output matches.

command.content: Goal: get your Meta models working again in omp and muse. Every API call returns "model not found" while dashboard Chat still works, so your next step is to send Meta the support ticket we drafted, with its reproduction steps. (disable recaps in /config)

<pasted_content id="fd98">
curl -X POST https://api.meta.ai/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: *** $MODEL_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{
  "model": "muse-spark-1.3-contributor",
  "input": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "why does the model work in this chat but not in api calls"
    },
    {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "This is the #1 API gotcha — you'''re almost never sending the *same* thing in the API as this chat is sending behind the scenes.

This chat app adds a lot of hidden stuff for you. When you call the API yourself, you have to add it manually.

Here are the differences that break 95% of people:

**1. The API is stateless, this chat is not**
Here I remember the whole conversation automatically.

In the API you have to re-send the full history every time:
```
system: ...
user: message 1
assistant: answer 1
user: message 2
```
If you only send the last `user:` message, it will act dumb / lose instructions.

**2. You'''re not using the same system prompt**
This chat runs with a hidden system instruction like `You are Muse Spark, a friendly AI Assistant...` plus formatting, safety, and style instructions.

In the API if your `system` is empty or different, you'''ll get a totally different personality / quality. Copy-paste the system prompt from here into your `system` parameter.

**3. You'''re not using the same model version**
This chat usually says "latest" and auto-updates.

API requires an exact ID like `muse-spark-...-001`, `gemini-1.5-pro-002`, `gpt-4o-2024-...`, etc. If you hardcoded an old pinned version, you'''re literally talking to a different model.

Check: What model ID are you passing in code?

**4. Default generation settings are different**
The chat UI uses tuned defaults for:
`temperature, top_p, top_k, max_output_tokens`

API SDKs use *their own* defaults, often `temperature=0` or `max_tokens= low`. That alone can make it look broken — too short, too repetitive, or too random.

Set them explicitly to match.

**5. This chat has tools turned on, your API doesn'''t**
This chat may have web search, code execution, file retrieval, function-calling enabled by default.

In the API those are OFF unless you pass `tools=[...]`, `grounding`, `code_interpreter`, etc. So tasks that need calculation / browsing will work here and fail there.

**6. Safety filters / project settings**
Playgrounds often run in "permissive for testing" mode. API calls run under *your* project settings with stricter safety blocks, quota limits, or no access to that model in that region. A silent block looks like "it doesn'''t work."

### How to make them identical

1. Look for a **View Code / Get Code / <>** button in this chat. Most playgrounds (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI Studio, Vertex) can export the *exact* Python / cURL it'''s using. Use that as your starting point, don'''t write it from scratch.
2. Log what you send: print the exact `model, messages, system_instruction, temperature, top_p, max_tokens, tools`
3. Start with a minimal repro: 1 system + 1 user message, temperature 0.7, max_tokens 1024, and expand from there.

> Tell me this and I can pinpoint it:
> 1. Which provider/SDK are you using?
> 2. What'''s the model name in the API call?
> 3. What happens in API — error message? Empty? Bad quality? Share your (redacted, no key) code snippet.

99% of the time once we compare the two payloads, the difference jumps out."
    }
  ],
  "stream": true,
  "temperature": 1,
  "max_output_tokens": 32000,
  "top_p": 1,
  "reasoning": {
    "effort": "medium"
  }
}'
